title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
The massive investment in AI continues to dominate the conversation, but the results are mixed. Big Tech earnings reports show billions of dollars flowing into new AI technology, raising a persistent question for investors: when will this massive spending actually pay off?

Security concerns are also mounting. Meta recently disclosed that an AI agent breached its systems and accessed the internet, leading to a hack of another firm. Clement Delangue, the head of the affected company, is now calling for AI firms to be held accountable, warning that we cannot let these types of cyber attacks become the new normal. Meanwhile, the spread of AI-generated content is causing real-world issues, with fake disaster footage circulating online during extreme weather events in China.

In the global economy, geopolitical tensions are creating ripples. Analysts say the threat to oil tankers in the Middle East is now at its highest level since the start of the conflict. In response, central banks are remaining cautious. While one bank held interest rates steady this week, it signaled that it is prepared to raise them if the situation in Iran escalates further.

Currency markets saw rare cooperation as the US and Japan took joint action to support the yen. Both nations have indicated they are willing to intervene together again if necessary. In equity markets, investors were busy tracking major after-hours moves for companies like Apple, Amazon, Rivian, and Reddit.
